h1: The 6 Best Garment Steamers Under $100 for Fast Wrinkle Removal, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Garment Steamer Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 garment steamers under $100 from Rowenta, Conair and PurSteam, scored on wattage, heat-up time, steam control and dual voltage.
summary: The Rowenta XCEL Steam Force DR2020 is the best garment steamer under $100, with 1875W and a 25 second heat-up at a price in the $25 to $50 bracket. The Rowenta Pure Force adds a larger tank and auto-off, the Conair 1875W handheld is the strong-steam alternative, and the small Conair Power Steam is the dual-voltage travel pick.
intro: Under $100 is where garment steamers get interesting, because the price gap between a throwaway and a keeper is small. The mistake is to buy the cheapest listing with the biggest wattage number and ignore how long it takes to be ready. A 1875W steamer that needs two minutes to warm up gets used less often than a 1500W one that is ready before the kettle boils.

The six steamers below are all handhelds that cost under $100, and each is judged on wattage, time to steam, extra controls and portability. Full-size irons with a steam button are a separate category, so they are not included here, even where they appear in the same search results.

products.name: Rowenta XCEL Steam Force Handheld Steamer 25-Sec Heat-Up, 1875W, DR2020
products.verdict: 1875W and a 25 second warm-up from a well-known steam brand, in the lower price bracket.
products.description:
The XCEL Steam Force DR2020 is a Rowenta handheld that draws 1875W and is ready in about 25 seconds. It costs less than $50, which makes it the cheapest branded 1875W steamer here.

Speed and power together are why it leads. Warm-up time is the spec that decides whether you reach for a steamer on a rushed morning, and a 25 second wait is shorter than most tidying routines. Compared with the Pure Force, you give up the stated tank size and auto-off, but you pay noticeably less. The listing does not name a tank capacity, so frequent users should expect to refill more often than with a bigger reservoir.

Buy it if you want strong steam, a quick start and a low price. Skip it if you want a named safety shut-off.
products.idealFor: Morning touch-ups on a tight schedule.
products.skipIf: You need an explicit safety shut-off.

products.name: Rowenta Pure Force 2in1 Steamer & Iron: Powerful 1875 Watts, Vertical
products.verdict: An XL 7.1oz tank with auto-off, working as a vertical steamer or a press.
products.description:
Rowenta's Pure Force 2-in-1 matches the 1875W power of the XCEL and adds an XL 7.1oz tank, an auto-off safety feature and a pressing mode. It works as a vertical steamer on hangers or as an iron on a flat surface.

Adding capacity and safety is the reason to pay more. A big tank lets one fill cover a full wardrobe, and the auto-off removes a common worry about leaving hot appliances plugged in. It trails the XCEL only on price and on the missing seconds figure for heat-up. The tank adds weight, so a long session will tire a wrist faster.

Buy it if you steam more than a couple of garments a week. Skip it if you want the lightest unit.
products.idealFor: Regular steaming of a full wardrobe.
products.skipIf: Weight and price are your top concerns.

products.name: Conair Handheld Garment Steamer for Clothes, Turbo ExtremeSteam 1875W
products.verdict: Conair's high-output handheld, built to push steam into heavier cloth.
products.description:
This Conair steamer runs at 1875W through its Turbo ExtremeSteam system, which the maker describes as penetrating. It is a one-handed model aimed at thicker garments.

Penetration matters on fabrics with depth, like a wool blazer, where surface steam leaves creases behind. That puts it level with the Rowenta on raw power, though the page omits a heat-up time and any tank figure, which keeps it below. Conair's wide retail presence means replacement parts are easy to find, which counts if you use it for years.

Buy it if heavier cloth is your main issue. Skip it if you want published tank or timing figures.
products.skipIf: You want a stated tank volume.

products.name: Conair 2-in-1 Handheld Steamer and Iron for Clothes, Turbo ExtremeSteam
products.verdict: 1875W of steam plus a flat plate to sharpen collars and cuffs.
products.description:
The Conair 2-in-1 adds a pressing plate to the 1875W Turbo ExtremeSteam handheld design. It lets you steam in the air and also flatten a seam against the surface.

A plate is useful for exactly two things, collars and hems, and it adds weight for everything else. That is why it sits fourth: those who want crisp edges benefit, while those who only steam hanging garments carry extra bulk. As with the other Conair, tank size is not listed.

Buy it if you need the occasional crisp edge and own no iron. Skip it if you already have one.
products.idealFor: Anyone without an iron who wants crisp edges.

products.name: PurSteam SteamWave Handheld Garment Steamer - Fast Heat-Up 3 Steam Settings
products.verdict: Three steam levels and a quick start in the cheapest bracket.
products.description:
The PurSteam SteamWave gives you three steam settings and a quick heat-up. It is a basic handheld at the $25 to $50 mark.

Choice of output is what sets it apart from the Conair and Rowenta, which run at one strength. A lower setting helps with silk and rayon, and a higher one works through cotton. The omissions are the usual ones for this tier: no wattage, no tank size and no timing figure on the page.

Buy it if you own both delicate and sturdy clothes. Skip it if you want stated power.

products.name: Conair Handheld Garment Steamer for Clothes - Power Steam: Small Size, Big
products.verdict: A small Conair steamer with dual voltage for use at home and abroad.
products.description:
This small Conair is a compact handheld with dual voltage for worldwide use. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

Dual voltage is the key trait: it lets you travel to Europe or Asia without a bulky converter, which a single-voltage steamer needs. The listing offers no wattage or heat-up figure, so we cannot say how strong the steam is. It is the least documented pick, hence the final place.

Buy it if you travel across voltage zones and want a Conair. Skip it if home use is your main need.

whatMatters.detail: A steamer should be ready in under 30 seconds, otherwise you will reach for the iron. The Rowenta XCEL lists 25 seconds, and several others list only fast. When a listing gives no time, assume it takes a minute or more.
Higher wattage boils water faster and keeps steam flowing on thick fabric. 1875W is the ceiling for a US household outlet on a handheld. Lower figures can still work, but expect slower passes.
Multiple settings protect delicates and speed up work on sturdy cloth. Three levels on the PurSteam give more control than a single strength. If you own silk, this matters more than raw power.
A bigger tank means fewer refills and a heavier body. A 7.1oz tank, as on the Pure Force, handles a full wardrobe, but your wrist feels it. Small tanks suit short touch-ups.
A 100-240V steamer works abroad with just a plug adapter. A 120V-only model risks burning out in a 230V socket. Look for dual voltage in the title if you travel internationally.

faq.a: For shirts, dresses and curtains, yes. A handheld heats fast and stores easily. Only a full-size steamer or iron will beat it for heavy daily volume.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one under $100?
faq.a: Chasing wattage and ignoring tank size. A tiny tank means constant refills, no matter how strong the steam. Check capacity or buy a model that lists it.

faq.q: Is the Pure Force worth it over the XCEL?
faq.a: If you steam often, yes. The larger tank and auto-off are the benefits. If you steam a few items a week, the XCEL does the job for less.

faq.q: How do I prevent water spots?
faq.a: Let the steamer heat fully before you start, and keep the head moving. Spitting water usually means it has not reached temperature yet.
Distilled water slows scale in hard-water areas. Tap water works but may leave deposits sooner. Descale with a vinegar mix when output drops.
Only for international travel. The small Conair Power Steam lists dual voltage, which saves carrying a converter. At home, any 120V model works.

finalTake: The Rowenta XCEL Steam Force DR2020 is the best garment steamer under $100, with 1875W, a 25 second warm-up and a price under $50. The Rowenta Pure Force is the right step up for a bigger tank and auto-off, while the Conair 1875W handheld handles heavy cloth. For delicates, the PurSteam's three settings help, and the small Conair is the dual-voltage option for trips. Match the tank to your wardrobe, not the wattage to the box.
